features.title: Notion OAuth login redirect
features.user_visible_behavior: Clicking 'Continue with Notion' sends the user to Notion's authorize screen.
verification: Start the server: cd server && npm start.
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n' http://localhost:3001/auth/
Assert HTTP 302 and the redirect URL points to api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with the configured client_id and redirect_uri.
evidence: server/api/auth.ts router.get('/') builds the authorize URL and calls res.redirect.
Covered by the ./init.sh baseline smoke check.
features.notes: Requires CLIENT_ID in .env.

features.title: OAuth callback upserts the user and redirects to /Dashboard
features.user_visible_behavior: After authorizing on Notion, the user is returned, their profile is stored, and they land on /Dashboard.
verification: Complete the Notion OAuth flow against http://localhost:3001/auth/callback with a valid code.
Verify a User row is upserted in Postgres (email, name, notionId, workspaceId, avatar).
Verify the browser is redirected to http://localhost:3000/Dashboard exactly once (no double-send).
evidence: Fixed double-send in server/api/auth.ts success branch: now `return res.redirect('http://localhost:3000/Dashboard')` only (removed the trailing res.json).
Error paths verified 2026-07-01: GET /auth/callback (no code) -> HTTP 400; GET /auth/callback?code=bogus -> HTTP 400 (Notion rejects), 0 occurrences of ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT in server log.
Baseline smoke check still passes after the change.
Manual OAuth run verified 2026-07-01: real Notion login redirects once to /Dashboard (404 there is expected until dash-001) and the User row was upserted correctly in Postgres.
features.notes: Passing. Success path confirmed by a manual Notion OAuth run (single 302 to /Dashboard + User upsert). The /Dashboard 404 is tracked separately by dash-001. (.env key is CLIENT_SECERT and the code matches it - left as-is on purpose.)

features.title: /Dashboard route renders after login
features.user_visible_behavior: An authenticated user sees the dashboard shell at /Dashboard instead of a 404.
verification: Start the frontend: npm run dev.
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/Dashboard
Assert HTTP 200 and the dashboard shell renders.
evidence: Added app/Dashboard/page.tsx: a server component (no data fetching) rendering the dashboard shell (header + placeholder region). Root app/layout.tsx wraps it.
Redirect target confirmed from source: server/api/auth.ts:81 returns res.redirect('http://localhost:3000/Dashboard') (capital-D), matching the app/Dashboard/ folder.
Verified 2026-07-01: ./init.sh baseline smoke check still PASSES (/auth/ -> 302, / -> 200).

Verified 2026-07-01: npm run dev, then curl http://localhost:3000/Dashboard -> HTTP 200 (was 404); response body contains the shell copy 'Edit conflicts detected across your Notion workspace.' Dev server torn down (port 3000 -> 000), clean state.
features.notes: Passing. Shell only (200 render) — listing conflicts is tracked by conflict-002, which will extend app/Dashboard/page.tsx once conflict-001 lands. No auth gate added on purpose (the verification curls /Dashboard with no session and expects 200).

features.title: Persist the Notion access token on the User during OAuth callback
features.user_visible_behavior: After a user authorizes on Notion, their access token is saved so the app can later read their workspace on their behalf.
verification: Add an accessToken field to the User model in prisma/schema.prisma and apply it to the DB (prisma migrate/db push), then npx prisma generate.
Update the prisma.user.upsert in server/api/auth.ts to store response.access_token on both create and update.
Complete an OAuth login (or exercise the upsert path) and verify the User row for that notionId has a non-null accessToken in Postgres.
Confirm ./init.sh baseline smoke check still passes and the token value is never written to logs or committed files.
evidence: Schema: added `accessToken String?` to the User model in prisma/schema.prisma (nullable, additive).

Migration drift resolved without data loss: the pre-existing `avatar` column was in the DB but not in any migration (would have forced `prisma migrate dev` to reset). Baselined it via migration 20260701120000_baseline_avatar marked `--applied` (recorded, not executed), then applied 20260701120100_add_user_access_token via `prisma migrate deploy`. `prisma migrate status` = up to date.
DB verified 2026-07-01: User table columns now include `accessToken`; the 1 existing User row survived (no data loss). Existing row has NULL accessToken (expected until the next login).
Code: server/api/auth.ts upsert now sets `accessToken: AccessToken` in both create and update; the success console.log still omits the token (not logged).

Baseline: ./init.sh smoke check PASSES after the change (client regenerated with the new field; /auth/ -> 302, / -> 200). NOTE: baseline does not exercise the callback success path, so it is supporting evidence only.

Primary evidence confirmed 2026-07-01: maintainer performed a manual Notion OAuth login and confirmed the access token is now saved on the User (non-null accessToken persisted via the callback upsert).
features.notes: Passing. Column added, data intact, upsert writes response.access_token on create and update, baseline passes, and a manual OAuth login confirmed the token is saved. Token stored plaintext (MVP; encryption-at-rest is out of scope, noted for future hardening). Treated as a secret: never logged. sync-001 can now use this per-user token.

features.title: Fetch and snapshot Notion pages/blocks per workspace
features.user_visible_behavior: After connecting, the user's Notion pages and block snapshots are stored for the workspace.
verification: Trigger a sync for a connected workspace.
Verify Page rows exist for the workspace (notionPageId, tittle, workspaceId).
Verify Snapshot rows are created linking blockId, pageId, and userId.
features.notes: Prisma models Page and Snapshot already exist in prisma/schema.prisma.

features.title: Detect concurrent edits and record Conflict rows
features.user_visible_behavior: When two users edit the same block around the same time, a conflict is recorded.
verification: Create two snapshots for the same blockId by two different users.
Run conflict detection.
Verify a Conflict row is created with pageId, blockId, user1Id, user2Id, and status='open'.
features.notes: Prisma model Conflict already exists (relations ConflictUser1/ConflictUser2).

features.title: Dashboard lists conflicts with status and resolver
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard shows detected conflicts with their status and who resolved them.
verification: Seed at least one Conflict row.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard.
Verify the conflict appears in the list with its status and resolvedBy value.
features.notes: Depends on dash-001 and conflict-001. Verification seeds a Conflict row directly, so it does not hard-depend on the GET /conflicts API (conflict-003).

features.title: 60-second polling snapshot engine
features.user_visible_behavior: Once a workspace is connected, its pages and block snapshots refresh automatically about every 60 seconds without any manual action.
verification: Start the server and connect a workspace so at least one Page row exists.
Confirm a setInterval (~60000ms) re-runs the sync-001 fetch+snapshot routine.
Wait for two intervals and verify new Snapshot rows (fresh createdAt) are appended for the same blocks.
Confirm the interval is set up once at server boot and does not stack duplicate timers on hot reload.
features.notes: Depends on sync-001. Phase 3 polling engine. Keep the token off logs. Consider guarding against overlapping runs if a sync takes longer than the interval.

features.title: Pages list with last-synced timestamp in the dashboard
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard lists every connected Notion page and shows when each was last synced.
verification: Seed or sync at least one Page row (tittle, workspaceId, notionPageId) with related Snapshot rows.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard.
Verify each page appears with its title and a last-synced time derived from the newest related Snapshot.createdAt.
features.notes: Depends on dash-001 and sync-001. Note the Page title field is spelled `tittle` in prisma/schema.prisma. 'Last synced' has no dedicated column; derive it from the most recent Snapshot.createdAt for the page.

features.title: Manual 'Sync Now' button
features.user_visible_behavior: A 'Sync Now' button on the dashboard triggers an immediate sync and the pages list/last-synced time updates.
verification: Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard and click 'Sync Now'.
Confirm it calls a backend sync endpoint that runs the sync-001 routine on demand.
Verify new Snapshot rows are written and the last-synced timestamp advances in the UI.
features.notes: Depends on sync-001 and sync-003. Needs a manual-trigger endpoint (e.g. POST /sync) that reuses the same routine as the sync-002 interval.

features.title: GET /conflicts returns unresolved conflicts
features.user_visible_behavior: The app can list all currently unresolved conflicts for a workspace.
verification: Seed at least one Conflict row with status='unresolved' and one with status='resolved'.
curl http://localhost:3001/conflicts
Assert only the unresolved conflict(s) are returned, including pageId, blockId, user1Id, user2Id, status, and createdAt.
features.notes: Depends on conflict-001. Standardizes on status values 'unresolved'/'resolved'. DISCREPANCY: existing conflict-001 verification uses status='open' while ALL_PHASE.md uses 'unresolved'|'resolved' — flagged for the maintainer to reconcile; new conflict entries use 'unresolved'/'resolved'.

features.title: PATCH /conflicts/:id/resolve marks a conflict resolved
features.user_visible_behavior: Resolving a conflict marks it resolved, records who resolved it and when, and removes it from the unresolved list.
verification: Seed a Conflict row with status='unresolved'.
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3001/conflicts/<id>/resolve with a resolver identity.
Verify the row now has status='resolved', a non-empty resolvedBy, and a resolvedAt timestamp.
Verify GET /conflicts (conflict-003) no longer returns that conflict.
features.notes: Depends on conflict-001 and conflict-003. SCHEMA NOTE: Conflict.resolvedBy is currently a non-null String (design intended nullable resolver). Detection (conflict-001) must therefore write a placeholder (e.g. "") on create, or the field should be made nullable via an additive migration — see auth-003 for the safe drift-handling pattern.

features.title: Side-by-side conflict view with Keep-User1 / Keep-User2 resolve buttons
features.user_visible_behavior: Each conflict shows User1's version next to User2's version with 'Keep User1' and 'Keep User2' buttons; resolving removes it from the list.
verification: Seed an unresolved Conflict row and open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard.
Verify the conflict renders both users' block versions side by side.
Click 'Keep User1' (or 'Keep User2') and confirm it calls PATCH /conflicts/:id/resolve.
Verify the resolved conflict disappears from the list without a full page reload.
features.notes: Depends on conflict-002, conflict-003, conflict-004. SCHEMA NOTE: the Conflict model has no user1Content/user2Content columns (ALL_PHASE.md design did). To show both versions, add those fields via an additive migration and populate them during detection (conflict-001), which in turn needs Snapshot.content — see the conflict-001 schema note.

features.title: Stat cards: total / resolved / unresolved / most active page
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard header shows summary cards for total conflicts, resolved, unresolved, and the most active page.
verification: Seed a mix of resolved and unresolved Conflict rows across at least two pages.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard.
Verify the four stat cards show correct counts and the page with the most conflicts as 'Most Active Page'.
features.notes: Depends on conflict-001. Counts derive from the Conflict table grouped by status and pageId.

features.title: Conflicts-over-time bar chart (Recharts)
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard shows a bar chart of conflicts over time.
verification: Seed Conflict rows with createdAt across several days.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard.
Verify a Recharts bar chart renders with bars bucketed by day matching the seeded data.
features.notes: Depends on conflict-001. Adds the `recharts` dependency to the root package.json.

features.title: Page health and team activity views
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard shows which pages have the most conflicts and which users cause the most conflicts.
verification: Seed Conflict rows spread across multiple pages and users.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard.
Verify a 'Page health' section ranks pages by conflict count and a 'Team activity' section ranks users by how many conflicts they are party to (user1Id or user2Id).
features.notes: Depends on conflict-001. Team activity counts a user via either the user1Id or user2Id side of a Conflict.

features.title: GET /team lists workspace members
features.user_visible_behavior: The app can list all users connected to the same workspace as one team.
verification: Seed two User rows sharing the same workspaceId.
curl http://localhost:3001/team for that workspace.
Assert both members are returned with name, email, and avatar; users from other workspaces are excluded.
features.notes: Phase 6 workspace concept: members are Users grouped by workspaceId (already on the User model).

features.title: Email notification when a new conflict is detected (nodemailer)
features.user_visible_behavior: When a new conflict is detected, the involved team members receive an email notification.
verification: Configure nodemailer with test SMTP credentials (e.g. an Ethereal/dev transport) via .env.
Trigger conflict detection so a new Conflict row is created.
Verify a notification email is sent to the involved users (capture the message id / preview URL from the transport).
features.notes: Depends on conflict-001. Adds `nodemailer`. SMTP creds are secrets — keep them in .env, never log or commit them.

features.title: Team members page (avatar, name, conflict count)
features.user_visible_behavior: A team page shows each member's avatar, name, and how many conflicts they are involved in.
verification: Seed workspace members and Conflict rows involving them.
Open the team members page in the frontend.
Verify each member shows avatar, name, and a conflict count (conflicts where they are user1 or user2).
features.notes: Depends on team-001 and conflict-001.

features.title: Filter conflicts by member and new-conflict notification badge
features.user_visible_behavior: The user can filter the conflicts list by team member and sees a badge on the dashboard when a new conflict arrives.
verification: Open the dashboard with conflicts involving multiple members.
Filter by one member and verify only conflicts involving that member remain.
Create a new conflict (or simulate one) and verify a notification badge appears on the dashboard.
features.notes: Depends on conflict-002/conflict-005 and team-001.

features.title: Error, loading, and empty states + mobile responsiveness
features.user_visible_behavior: The app handles errors gracefully, shows loading indicators while fetching, shows friendly empty states, and is usable on mobile.
verification: Load the dashboard with no conflicts and verify an empty state (e.g. 'No conflicts detected 🎉').
Simulate a failing backend call and verify an error state renders instead of a crash.
Verify loading indicators appear during data fetches.
Check the dashboard at a mobile viewport width (~375px) and confirm the layout stays usable.
features.notes: Phase 7 polish. Broad by nature — verify per screen rather than a single assertion.

features.title: Seed demo data for showcase
features.user_visible_behavior: A seed script populates realistic demo users, pages, snapshots, and conflicts so the dashboard looks populated for a demo.
verification: Run the seed script against a clean database.
Verify User, Page, Snapshot, and Conflict rows (mix of resolved/unresolved) are created.
Open http://localhost:3000/Dashboard and confirm the stat cards, chart, and lists render with the seeded data.
features.notes: Phase 7. Keep the seed idempotent/reset-safe so it can be re-run for demos.

features.title: Deploy to Supabase + Render + Vercel
features.user_visible_behavior: The app is reachable at a public URL: frontend on Vercel, backend on Render, database on Supabase.
verification: Provision the Postgres database on Supabase and run migrations against it.
Deploy the Express server to Render with the required env vars set (no secrets committed).
Deploy the Next.js frontend to Vercel pointed at the deployed backend.
Complete a live Notion OAuth login end to end and confirm the dashboard loads with real data.
features.notes: Phase 7. Update the Notion OAuth redirect_uri to the deployed callback URL. All secrets via platform env vars, never committed.
